artist_biography: Aphex Twin is the stage name of British electronic musician Richard D. James, known for influential work spanning ambient, techno, IDM and experimental electronic music.
Boards of Canada are a Scottish electronic duo known for nostalgic melodies, hazy analogue textures and atmospheric productions that became highly influential in IDM and ambient music.
Autechre are a British electronic duo whose complex rhythms, abstract sound design and algorithmic approach have made them central figures in experimental electronic music.
DJ Shadow is an American producer and DJ known for sample-based instrumental hip-hop, cinematic beatmaking and the landmark album Endtroducing.....
Daft Punk were a French electronic duo whose blend of house, disco, funk and pop helped shape modern dance music and global electronic culture.
Massive Attack are a British group from Bristol widely associated with the development of trip-hop, combining electronic production, dub, hip-hop and soulful vocals.
The Chemical Brothers are a British electronic duo known for big beat, psychedelic production and energetic dance tracks that brought electronic music to a wider rock and pop audience.
Portishead are a British band from Bristol known for dark, cinematic trip-hop built around haunting vocals, hip-hop-inspired beats and atmospheric production.
Moby is an American musician and producer known for electronic music that blends techno, ambient, rock, gospel and pop influences.
The Prodigy are a British electronic group known for high-energy rave, breakbeat and big beat music that crossed electronic dance culture with punk attitude.
Air are a French duo known for elegant electronic pop, downtempo grooves, vintage synthesizers and cinematic arrangements.
Burial is the stage name of a British electronic producer known for atmospheric, fragmented UK garage, dubstep and haunting urban soundscapes.
Bonobo is the stage name of British musician and producer Simon Green, known for downtempo electronic music, organic instrumentation and richly layered arrangements.
Four Tet is the stage name of British producer Kieran Hebden, whose work blends electronic music with folk, jazz, house and experimental influences.
Caribou is the project of Canadian musician Dan Snaith, known for melodic electronic music that combines psychedelia, dance rhythms and detailed production.
Jamie xx is a British producer, DJ and member of The xx, known for minimalist electronic music, house influences and inventive sampling.
Flying Lotus is an American producer and musician known for experimental electronic music that blends hip-hop, jazz, psychedelia and futuristic beatmaking.
Kraftwerk are a pioneering German electronic group whose minimalist rhythms, synthesizers and machine-inspired aesthetic had a major influence on electronic, pop and hip-hop music.
New Order are a British band formed after Joy Division, known for combining post-punk songwriting with synthesizers, sequencers and dance-music rhythms.
Depeche Mode are a British electronic band known for dark synth-pop, memorable melodies and an influential blend of electronic production and alternative rock.
Pet Shop Boys are a British synth-pop duo known for sophisticated electronic pop, witty lyrics and a long-running influence on dance and pop music.
Goldfrapp are a British electronic duo known for shifting between cinematic electronic music, glam-influenced synth-pop and atmospheric art pop.
The Smashing Pumpkins are an American alternative rock band known for layered guitars, dynamic songwriting and a distinctive mix of grunge, psychedelia and dream pop.
Underworld are a British electronic group known for progressive dance music, hypnotic rhythms and long-form tracks that became influential in techno and club culture.
Orbital are a British electronic duo known for melodic techno, intricate live performances and a major role in the development of 1990s electronic dance music.
Justice are a French electronic duo known for distorted synths, rock-influenced production and a powerful electro-house sound.
Moderat are a German electronic group formed by Modeselektor and Apparat, blending emotive vocals, detailed sound design and club-oriented rhythms.
Apparat is the stage name of German musician Sascha Ring, known for atmospheric electronic music, detailed sound design and emotionally rich compositions.
Röyksopp are a Norwegian electronic duo known for melodic synth-pop, downtempo production and polished dance music.
The Knife were a Swedish electronic duo known for experimental synth-pop, distinctive vocals and unconventional approaches to rhythm, performance and identity.
Hot Chip are a British electronic band known for combining synth-pop, indie music and dance-floor rhythms with warm, playful songwriting.
Disclosure are a British electronic duo known for house and UK garage-inspired production that helped bring a new wave of dance music into mainstream pop.
Fleetwood Mac are a British-American rock band known for melodic songwriting, vocal harmonies and a long career spanning blues rock, soft rock and pop.
Nirvana were an American rock band whose raw songwriting and breakthrough success helped bring grunge and alternative rock into the global mainstream.
Pink Floyd were a British rock band known for progressive and psychedelic music, ambitious concept albums, studio experimentation and elaborate live presentation.
Queen were a British rock band known for theatrical performances, powerful vocals and an eclectic catalogue combining rock, pop, opera and other styles.
Amy Winehouse was a British singer-songwriter known for her distinctive voice and a modern blend of soul, jazz and R&B.
Stevie Wonder is an American singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist whose innovative work in soul, funk, R&B and pop has influenced generations of musicians.
Marvin Gaye was an American soul singer and songwriter known for expressive vocals, socially conscious themes and landmark recordings for Motown.
Miles Davis was an American trumpeter and bandleader whose constant musical evolution helped shape bebop, cool jazz, modal jazz and jazz fusion.
John Coltrane was an American saxophonist and composer whose innovative improvisation and spiritual approach made him one of the most influential figures in jazz.
Bob Marley & The Wailers were a Jamaican reggae group whose music helped bring reggae and Rastafarian themes to an international audience.
Red Hot Chili Peppers are an American rock band known for combining funk, alternative rock and punk with energetic performances and melodic songwriting.
Metallica are an American heavy metal band known for fast, powerful riffing, ambitious songwriting and a major role in the development of thrash metal.
Arctic Monkeys are a British rock band known for sharp lyricism, evolving guitar-driven styles and a progression from indie rock to broader alternative influences.
Adele is a British singer-songwriter known for powerful vocals, emotionally direct songwriting and globally successful soul-influenced pop ballads.
Michael Jackson was an American singer, songwriter and performer whose innovative pop, R&B and dance recordings made him one of the most influential entertainers in modern music.
The Beatles were a British rock band whose songwriting, studio experimentation and cultural impact transformed popular music in the 1960s and beyond.
David Bowie was a British singer, songwriter and performer known for constant reinvention, influential personas and music spanning rock, pop, soul and electronic experimentation.
Led Zeppelin were a British rock band known for powerful guitar-driven music that blended blues, folk and hard rock and strongly influenced heavy rock.
The Clash were a British punk band known for politically charged songwriting and a broad musical palette that incorporated reggae, ska, rockabilly and funk.
The Strokes are an American rock band whose concise guitar-driven songs and distinctive style played a major role in the early-2000s garage rock revival.
Johnny Cash was an American singer-songwriter known for his deep voice, narrative songwriting and influential work across country, folk, gospel and rock.
Carole King is an American singer-songwriter whose intimate songwriting and piano-led style helped define the singer-songwriter era of the 1970s.
Joni Mitchell is a Canadian singer-songwriter known for poetic lyrics, inventive guitar tunings and an evolving style spanning folk, rock and jazz.
Aretha Franklin was an American singer and pianist celebrated as one of the defining voices of soul music, known for powerful performances and gospel-rooted expression.
Prince was an American singer, songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist known for a distinctive fusion of funk, rock, pop, R&B and electronic music.
Black Sabbath are a British rock band whose heavy riffs, dark themes and powerful sound were foundational to the development of heavy metal.
Guns N' Roses are an American hard rock band known for blues-influenced guitar work, powerful vocals and a raw sound that became hugely successful in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
B.B. King was an American blues guitarist and singer known for his expressive vibrato, lyrical guitar phrasing and enormous influence on blues and rock musicians.
Bob Dylan is an American singer-songwriter whose poetic lyrics, folk roots and constant reinvention have had a profound influence on popular music and songwriting.
Santana are an American rock band led by guitarist Carlos Santana, known for blending Latin rhythms, blues, jazz and rock with a distinctive guitar sound.
Taylor Swift is an American singer-songwriter known for narrative songwriting and a career that has evolved across country, pop, folk and alternative styles.
Beyoncé is an American singer, songwriter and performer known for powerful vocals, ambitious visual projects and music spanning R&B, pop, dance and soul.
Radiohead are a British band known for adventurous alternative rock and experimental music that incorporates electronic textures, unusual structures and atmospheric production.
Pearl Jam are an American rock band associated with the Seattle grunge movement, known for powerful live performances and emotionally direct songwriting.
Green Day are an American punk rock band known for melodic, energetic songs that helped bring punk-influenced music into the mainstream.
Foo Fighters are an American rock band founded by Dave Grohl, known for melodic alternative rock, powerful guitars and an extensive live career.
Lauryn Hill is an American singer, rapper and songwriter known for blending hip-hop, soul and R&B with introspective and socially aware lyricism.
Etta James was an American singer known for a powerful, emotionally expressive voice and recordings that crossed blues, soul, R&B and jazz.
Herbie Hancock is an American pianist and composer whose innovative career has ranged from acoustic jazz to funk, fusion and electronic experimentation.
The Cure are a British band known for atmospheric post-punk, gothic rock and melodic alternative music led by the distinctive songwriting and voice of Robert Smith.
Dolly Parton is an American singer-songwriter known for classic country songwriting, distinctive vocals and a long career spanning music, film and popular culture.
Tracy Chapman is an American singer-songwriter known for socially conscious lyrics, acoustic arrangements and a distinctive folk-rock style.
Alanis Morissette is a Canadian-American singer-songwriter known for emotionally direct alternative rock and confessional songwriting.
ABBA are a Swedish pop group known for polished songwriting, rich vocal harmonies and a catalogue of internationally successful pop and disco songs.
Elton John is a British singer, pianist and songwriter known for melodic pop-rock, theatrical performances and a decades-long partnership with lyricist Bernie Taupin.
The Rolling Stones are a British rock band whose blues-rooted sound, songwriting and live performances made them one of the longest-running and most influential groups in rock history.
Bruce Springsteen is an American singer-songwriter known for narrative rock songs about working life, community and personal struggle, often performed with the E Street Band.
The Doors were an American rock band known for psychedelic and blues-influenced music, distinctive keyboards and the charismatic vocals of Jim Morrison.
AC/DC are an Australian rock band known for direct, riff-driven hard rock, powerful live performances and a highly recognizable guitar sound.
Iron Maiden are a British heavy metal band known for melodic twin-guitar work, epic songwriting and a major influence on the global metal scene.
The Black Keys are an American rock duo known for blues-inspired garage rock, gritty guitar tones and a stripped-down approach that later expanded into polished alternative rock.
Norah Jones is an American singer, songwriter and pianist known for a warm, understated style blending jazz, pop, folk and country influences.
Frank Sinatra was an American singer and actor known for sophisticated phrasing, classic interpretations of popular songs and a major role in 20th-century vocal pop.
Ray Charles was an American singer, pianist and songwriter whose fusion of gospel, blues, jazz and R&B helped shape the development of soul music.
Shakira is a Colombian singer-songwriter known for a distinctive voice and a global pop career blending Latin, rock, dance and Middle Eastern influences.
Buena Vista Social Club is a celebrated Cuban music project that brought veteran Cuban musicians and traditional styles such as son and bolero to a global audience.
Maroon 5 are an American pop-rock band known for melodic songwriting, funk and R&B influences and a long run of mainstream pop hits.
Coldplay are a British band known for melodic alternative rock, atmospheric production and an evolving sound that increasingly incorporates pop and electronic elements.
Lana Del Rey is an American singer-songwriter known for cinematic pop, melancholic songwriting and imagery inspired by Americana and classic popular culture.
Florence + the Machine are a British indie rock group led by Florence Welch, known for dramatic vocals, expansive arrangements and a blend of rock, soul and art pop.
